decisive_items: brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma
central infiltrate involving all corneal layers and a peripheral infiltrate concentrated in the deep stroma
His postoperative course was initially uneventful under topical and systemic corticosteroids
response.rationale: Deep stromal brown multilobular lesions with no epithelial defect and corticosteroid use favor fungal keratitis; immune-mediated keratitis is less specific and lacks supporting signs.

rejected.why: Corticosteroid use is a risk factor but not a diagnosis; no direct evidence of steroid-induced keratitis.
Prior Thaumetopoea infection resolved before surgery and current findings are not typical of active caterpillar keratitis.
Immune-mediated keratitis is plausible but lacks specific features; deep infiltrates and brown lesions are more consistent with fungal infection.
